answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond, locked until its work is audited and for a challenge window afterward. When a verifier proves two identities are controlled by the same key or coordinated account, the protocol can slash their bonds and reject their duplicate claims. Spreading a fake swarm across many identities therefore requires tying up real capital in every one, while risking its loss; rotating names is cheap, but replenishing quartz, quill, and jade cannot evade the bond requirement.
